content.text: The rule seems to be about flood-filling from the outside with 3, so any fully enclosed regions bounded by lines get marked as 2. I'm realizing there's no actual test input grid given here to apply this rule to, so I don't have anything concrete to submit yet.

Rows 0-3 all connect to the outer boundary, so those free cells are all 3. Now I'm tracing the left-side region (cols 0-4) down through row 4-21, checking where it connects to the outside via row4's open columns 0,1, and identifying spots like row14 and row18 cols 3-4 where walls might cut off small pockets.

I'm also checking the right column (24) and cols 23-24 near rows 5-8, confirming they stay open to the outer flood, then moving to the tricky interior region between cols 6-10 in rows 5-8 to see if it's sealed off by walls above and below.

Tracing further, I see this region actually leaks through row9 at cols6-9 (which are free despite walls elsewhere in that row), connecting down into rows10-13 and expanding sideways to cols12-15 where col11's wall gaps at rows12-13 open a path—so I'm carefully mapping how far this connected area extends before hitting the row14 wall boundary and the col11 barrier on the right.

Cols17-21 rows5-8 also enclosed similarly → 2. But row14 breaks the pattern: walls span cols3-19 only, leaving cols20-24 open, which could let that area escape to the border - I need to check if that leaks out.

Then cols23,24 in rows10-12 connect straight to the outside since row9's wall only covers cols10-23 for col23, but col24 stays open, so this region touches the border and doesn't count as enclosed.

Now I'm shifting focus to rows15 and below, working out how row14's wall (cols3-19) splits the space into a left section (cols0-4), a gap at col5, a middle section (cols6-15), another wall at col16, and an open area from cols17-24 - then checking what row17's wall pattern (col5 and cols12-20) does to that layout.

Everything below row14 seems to funnel into region 3 through the open corridors down to row20 and out. I want to double-check the rows5-8 cols6-10 area I labeled as region 2, tracing downward through rows10-13 to confirm it doesn't actually leak into the row14 wall gap and merge with region 3.

I'm now mapping out the wall boundaries row by row to confirm which columns get marked 2 versus 3, checking col16 blocks at rows12-13 and building the col ranges for each row segment.
